# Coding Agent Session Guide

## Package Manager

**Default to Bun** (`bun`) — but check the lockfile first (`bun.lock`/`bun.lockb`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `package-lock.json`); many projects use pnpm or npm instead:
- npm: `bun install` instead of `npm install`
- npx: `bunx` instead of `npx`
- Scripts: `bun run <script>` instead of `npm run <script>`

## Your LLM Wiki

A persistent knowledge base tracks all project work. You are expected to log significant activities.

**Wiki Location**: `/Users/jvent/Dev/ai-agents-and-skills/llm-wiki`

**Key Files**:
- `log.md` — Append-only activity log (ingest, query, session summaries)
- `index.md` — Content catalog (entities, concepts, sources, synthesis)
- `AGENTS.md` — Full schema and conventions

**Wiki Structure**:
```
llm-wiki/
├── log.md                    # Activity log (append-only)
├── index.md                  # Catalog of all pages
├── wiki/
│   ├── entities/             # People, organizations, projects
│   ├── concepts/             # Patterns, methodologies, techniques
│   ├── sources/              # Document summaries
│   └── synthesis/            # Cross-cutting analyses
```

---

## Session Logging Workflow

### At Session Start
- Read the last 40 lines of `log.md` (`tail -40`); the file is 250 KB+, never read it whole
- Check `index.md` for relevant project context

### During Session
- Log significant actions to `log.md`:
  ```
  ## [YYYY-MM-DD] session | Project: Brief Description
  - Completed: [what was done]
  - Next: [what remains]
  - Blockers: [if any]
  ```

### At Session End
- Write a session summary to `log.md`
- Update relevant entity/concept pages if new patterns discovered
- Update `index.md` if new pages were created

### Log Entry Format
```markdown
## [YYYY-MM-DD] session | Project Name — Brief description
- Completed: [3-5 bullet points of significant work]
- Decisions: [architectural choices, trade-offs made]
- Next Steps: [immediate next actions]
- Notes: [anything worth remembering]
```

---

## Port Conflicts

When a `dev` or `start` command fails with `EADDRINUSE` (port already in use), automatically retry on the next port without asking. Increment by 1 until a free port is found (e.g. 3000 → 3001 → 3002). Pass the port via the `-p` flag or `PORT` env var depending on the tool.

---

## Git Push Rules

Never push directly to `main`/`master` — always work on a branch and open a PR,
even if explicitly asked to push straight to main. Ask first if a push to
main seems necessary.

---

## Next.js 16 — Proxy (formerly Middleware)

Next.js 16 renamed `middleware.ts` → `proxy.ts`. Key changes:

### Migration
- Rename `middleware.ts` → `proxy.ts`
- Export: `middleware` → `proxy`
- Config: `skipMiddlewareUrlNormalize` → `skipProxyUrlNormalize`
- Codemod: `npx @next/codemod@canary middleware-to-proxy .`

### Proxy Matcher Examples
```ts
// Basic
matcher: '/about/:path*'

// Exclude internals
matcher: '/((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico).*)'

// Protected paths
matcher: ['/dashboard/:path*', '/api/protected/:path*']
```

### Best Practices
- Edge runtime only—keep lightweight
- Use for routing/auth gating; verify data access in handlers
- BFF/API proxying via rewrites

## When to Log

| Action | Log Type |
|--------|----------|
| Project setup complete | `session` |
| Feature implemented | `session` |
| Bug fixed (nontrivial) | `session` |
| Architectural decision | `session` + concept page |
| New project discovered | `session` + entity page |
| Research/thinking | `query` or `session` |
| Lint/health check | `lint` |

---

## Shell Command Rules (Token Hygiene)

These rules prevent context pollution from expensive shell patterns:

- **NEVER** use `psql "postgresql://..."` — use `mcp__supabase__execute_sql` instead
- **NEVER** use `curl -s http://localhost:*` — use WebFetch or the Supabase MCP tools
- **NEVER** use `python3 -c "..."` inline — write to `/tmp/script.py` and execute that
- **NEVER** use `node -e "..."` inline — write to `/tmp/script.mjs` and execute that
- **NEVER** use heredoc scripts (`python3 << 'EOF'`) — write to file first, same as above

**Why:** Inline scripts (128 `node -e`, 100 `python3 -c`, 70 heredocs) flood context with escaped strings. Each `psql` call (60) and `curl` call (64) bypasses MCP tooling and carries raw output into context. Use the right tool and the output is capped automatically.

---

## Browser Automation (Token Hygiene)

**Default to the `agent-browser` CLI** (`/opt/homebrew/bin/agent-browser`, installed system-wide) over the `claude-in-chrome` / `chrome-devtools` MCP tools for ad-hoc browser verification (checking a deployed page, testing a login flow, confirming a UI fix rendered correctly).

```bash
agent-browser open <url>       # launch + navigate
agent-browser snapshot         # accessibility tree with @refs — pipe through rg for just what you need
agent-browser click @e1        # or a CSS/XPath selector
agent-browser fill @e2 "text"
agent-browser screenshot [path]
agent-browser read             # rendered text of the active tab
agent-browser close
```

**Why:** terser output than MCP round-trips (most commands return one line, e.g. `✓ Done`), no fixed schema-load cost per call, and snapshots can be filtered before they ever hit context (`agent-browser snapshot | rg -i button`). It also self-reports covering elements on a blocked click (`✗ Element covered by <a.absolute.inset-0>...`) which MCP click tools don't surface as cleanly.

**Keep using the MCP browser tools when:** the task needs `claude-in-chrome`'s access to the user's *actual logged-in browser* (their real cookies/session, not a fresh automated one), or needs a capability `agent-browser` doesn't have (e.g. `chrome-devtools`'s performance tracing/Lighthouse).

---

## Conventions

- Use `[[page-id|Display Text]]` for internal wiki links
- Frontmatter required on new pages: `title`, `type`, `tags`, `created`, `updated`
- Kebab-case filenames: `project-name.md`
- Update `index.md` within 24hrs of creating new pages

# graphify
- **graphify** (`~/.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`) - any input to knowledge graph. Trigger: `/graphify`
When the user types `/graphify`, use the installed graphify skill or instructions before doing anything else.

# unslop
- **unslop** (`~/.claude/skills/unslop/SKILL.md`) - cut AI tells from writing. Trigger: `/unslop`
Apply the unslop rules to every response and every document you write, without being asked.
No em dashes. Say what a thing does, not how it feels. Cut filler, puffery, and hedging.
Read the skill file for the full pattern list when writing anything longer than a few lines.

# autonomy
Default to acting, not asking.

- **Just fix it, no permission needed:** bugs found on the way to the real task,
  anything you broke, anything that restores previously-working behaviour, cleanup
  and dead files inside the repo, stale copies of things you just changed. Report it
  after in one line, under a "also fixed" heading.
- **Ask first, always:** deleting data, force-push, rotating credentials, anything
  that costs money, anything irreversible outside the repo.
- **Never end a message with "want me to X?"** If X is worth doing, do it now. If it
  isn't, drop it silently. If it is genuinely Jesse's call, state your recommendation
  and proceed on it unless told otherwise.
- **One exception:** if two readings of the request produce materially different work,
  ask once, before starting. Not at the end.
- Noticing a problem is not a reason to raise it. Fix it, or let it go.

# plan-first
Default to planning before building. For any task that touches more than one file,
changes behaviour, or has more than one reasonable approach: enter plan mode (EnterPlanMode),
read the code the change touches, write the plan (files, steps, checks), then execute it.
Skip the plan only for one-line fixes, typos, and pure questions. Never skip because the
task "looks simple". A UserPromptSubmit hook injects PLAN REQUIRED on non-trivial prompts; obey it.

# artifacts
Never create an Artifact (published HTML page) unless Jesse asks for one by name in the
prompt. Reports, summaries, plans, and comparisons go in the terminal reply. A PreToolUse
hook enforces this; do not try to route around it.

# issues
When Jesse says "issues" (outstanding, open, close out, triage), that means GitHub
issues: run `gh issue list --state open` first and work from that list. Never treat
a local doc, plan, or gate file as the issue tracker. Ask only if `gh` returns nothing.

# RTK - Rust Token Killer

**Usage**: Token-optimized CLI proxy (60-90% savings on dev operations)

## Meta Commands (always use rtk directly)

```bash
rtk gain              # Show token savings analytics
rtk gain --history    # Show command usage history with savings
rtk discover          # Analyze Claude Code history for missed opportunities
rtk proxy <cmd>       # Execute raw command without filtering (for debugging)
```

## Installation Verification

```bash
rtk --version         # Should show: rtk X.Y.Z
rtk gain              # Should work (not "command not found")
which rtk             # Verify correct binary
```

⚠️ **Name collision**: If `rtk gain` fails, you may have reachingforthejack/rtk (Rust Type Kit) installed instead.

## Hook-Based Usage

All other commands are automatically rewritten by the Claude Code hook.
Example: `git status` → `rtk git status` (transparent, 0 tokens overhead)

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Workspace Overview

`/Users/jvent/Dev` is a **multi-project workspace** (not a single codebase). Projects are prefixed numerically (`00-`, `01-`, etc.) for active projects. Archived or experimental work lives in `_archive/`, `_data/`, `_docs/`, and `_scripts/`.

Most projects follow one of two patterns:
- **Vite SPA** — React + TypeScript, Supabase backend, Tailwind + shadcn/ui
- **Turborepo monorepo** — `apps/` + `packages/` structure, multiple frontends sharing a `packages/database`, `packages/ui`, `packages/ai`

## Standard Stack

- **Frontend:** React + TypeScript, Vite (SPAs) or Next.js App Router (full-stack)
- **Styling:** Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui
- **State:** Zustand for global state
- **Database:** Supabase (PostgreSQL + pgvector + Edge Functions)
- **AI:** Google Gemini (2.0 Flash, 2.5 Pro)
- **Monorepos:** Turborepo + pnpm workspaces
- **Healthcare data:** DuckDB + OMOP CDM v5.4

## Common Commands

Most projects use one of these package managers — check the lockfile (`pnpm-lock.yaml`, `bun.lock`, `package-lock.json`). Supabase local dev: `supabase start` / `db push` / `functions serve`. Turborepo monorepos: `pnpm --filter <app-name> dev`, `pnpm turbo build`.

## Code Conventions

- **TypeScript:** 2-space indent, camelCase, no `any` — define interfaces for everything
- **Python:** 4-space indent, snake_case, PEP 8
- **Naming:** Capability-based, not abstract — `DocumentUpload` not `InspirationHub`
- **Commits:** Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:` etc.)
- **No over-engineering:** Simple solutions, no premature abstractions, no gratuitous comments

## Modern CLI Substitutions (Token Hygiene)

Prefer these modern tools over legacy commands — their default output is leaner,
cutting context tokens at the source. All are installed system-wide.

| Prefer | Instead of | Notes |
|--------|-----------|-------|
| `rg`   | `grep`    | recursive **by default**; `rg -n pattern`; no `-r`/`--include` needed |
| `fd`   | `find`    | regex first arg: `fd '\.ts$'`; by ext: `fd -e ts`; no `-name`/`-type f` boilerplate |
| `bat`  | `cat`     | `bat --plain file` for raw; but **prefer the Read tool** for full files |
| `eza`  | `ls`      | `eza -la --git`; tree: `eza -T` |
| `sd`   | `sed`     | `sd 'old' 'new' file` (regex); no `/` delimiter pain |
| `dust` | `du`      | `dust -d 2` (depth); visual disk usage |
| `duf`  | `df`      | clean table; `duf --only local` |
| `procs`| `ps`      | `procs <name>` to filter; far less noise than `ps aux` |
| `xh`   | `curl`    | ad-hoc HTTP test only — never localhost/internal; use WebFetch or MCP per rules above |
| `btm`  | `top`     | **interactive only** — never inside the agent loop |
| `z`    | `cd`      | zoxide frecency jump (init'd in shell); Bash tool uses absolute paths anyway |

**Rules:**
- Searching → `rg` / `fd`, never `grep` / `find`.
- Reading a whole file → **Read tool first**, not `bat` / `cat`. `bat` only for a quick syntax-highlighted peek.
- `btm` / `procs` / `dust` / `duf` are heavy or interactive — run once, never in tight loops.
- `xh` is for manual HTTP debugging only. For URLs → WebFetch; for Supabase → MCP tools; for localhost → WebFetch (never raw `curl`).

## Supabase Patterns

Most projects use a consistent pattern:
- `supabase/migrations/` — schema history (never edit old files)
- `supabase/functions/` — Edge Functions (Deno runtime)
- `src/lib/supabase.ts` — typed Supabase client
- `src/lib/api.ts` — RPC wrappers and data access functions
- Row Level Security enabled on all user-facing tables

## Turborepo Monorepo Structure

```
apps/
  dashboard/    # Admin/creator interface (Vite)
  marketplace/  # Public-facing (Next.js)
packages/
  ai/           # Gemini/LLM integration
  database/     # Supabase client + generated types
  ui/           # Shared shadcn/ui components
supabase/
  migrations/
  functions/
```

## Scaffolds & Scripts

- `scaffolds/` — reusable project templates
- `_scripts/` — workspace-level utilities (`repo_analyzer.sh`, `code_analyzer.sh`, `build_call_graph.py`)
- `_docs/` — cross-project documentation and analysis outputs

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What This Is

A Supabase developer tool built with Next.js 16 App Router. Connect to multiple Supabase projects and inspect schema, RLS policies, edge functions, run SQL, view indexes/triggers, profile tables, and more. Has a Demo Mode that works without a real connection.

## Commands

```bash
# Dev server (Bun, port 3000)
bun dev

# Build (outputs standalone bundle)
bun run build

# Production start
bun start

# Lint
bun run lint
```

No environment variables are required to run the app. There is no local database — no Prisma, no SQLite. See `.env.example` for optional config (LLM API keys, S3/Iceberg pre-fill).

## Architecture

**Single-page shell + dynamic panels.** `src/app/page.tsx` is the main shell — it manages navigation, connection selection, and renders the active panel. All feature panels (`src/components/*.tsx`) are dynamically imported with `next/dynamic` for lazy loading.

**API routes** (`src/app/api/`) are the backend. Each route reads connection credentials directly from the request body and proxies calls to Supabase. There is no server-side database — credentials come from the client on each request.

**API route map:**
- `agent/chat/` — server proxy for LLM calls (OpenAI / Anthropic / Google); injects API key server-side
- `catalog/setup` — creates `catalog_tables` + `catalog_columns` tables in the connected project
- `catalog/profile` — runs data profiling queries (row counts, null %, distinct, min/max)
- `catalog/load` — retrieves stored catalog metadata
- `catalog/commit` — saves AI-generated descriptions back to catalog
- `connections/` — CRUD for stored connections (credentials validated client-side)
- `connections/[id]/health` — four-point health check (URL, anon key, access token, service role key)
- `schema/` — introspects tables, columns, foreign keys (Management API SQL → PostgREST OpenAPI → REST discovery)
- `rls/` — RLS enable status + policies
- `sql/` — execute arbitrary SQL via Management API
- `tables/rows/` — fetch paginated row data via PostgREST (prefers `serviceRoleKey` to bypass RLS)
- `edge-functions/` + `invoke/` — list and call edge functions
- `database/indexes/`, `triggers/`, `views-functions/` — Management API SQL introspection
- `project/` — project metadata
- `realtime-token/` — generate a Realtime WebSocket auth token
- `storage/` — bucket/folder browsing via Supabase Storage API
- `storage/download/` — proxy for file download

**State** is managed by two Zustand stores, both with `persist` middleware to `localStorage`:
- `src/store/supabase-store.ts` (key: `supabase-debug-storage`) — connections, activeConnectionId, activePanel, SQL history, schema snapshots, migration history, latency records. Transient state (loaded tables, RLS statuses, loading/error flags) is not persisted.
- `src/store/agent-store.ts` — LLM provider config (provider, model, baseURL, apiKey), maxSteps. Transient: messages, currentTask, agentStatus.

**Two Supabase auth paths:**
- Management API (`https://api.supabase.com/v1/projects/{ref}/...`) — requires `accessToken` (`sbp_...`). Used for schema introspection, SQL execution, RLS queries, data catalog profiling.
- PostgREST (`{supabaseUrl}/rest/v1/...`) — requires `serviceRoleKey` or `anonKey`. New opaque key formats (`sb_secret_`, `sb_publishable_`) are exchanged for JWTs via `/auth/v1/token?grant_type=anonymous` before use. See `getValidApiKey()` in `supabase-helpers.ts`.

**AI Agent** (`src/agent/`) — a PageAgent that autonomously queries schemas, runs SQL, inspects RLS, and debugs across multiple steps. Tools are defined in `supabase-tools.ts`. LLM calls are proxied through `/api/agent/chat` so API keys never reach the browser.

**Types** are centralized in `src/lib/supabase-types.ts`. Import all shared interfaces from there.

## Key Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `src/app/page.tsx` | Main shell, nav, connection management UI |
| `src/store/supabase-store.ts` | Main Zustand store (connections, SQL history, snapshots, latency) |
| `src/store/agent-store.ts` | Agent Zustand store (LLM config, messages) |
| `src/lib/supabase-types.ts` | All shared TypeScript interfaces |
| `src/lib/supabase-helpers.ts` | Server-side functions calling Supabase APIs |
| `src/lib/supabase-client.ts` | Client-side `createClient` factory |
| `src/lib/demo-data.ts` | Mock data for Demo Mode |
| `src/agent/supabase-tools.ts` | Agent tool definitions |
| `src/agent/use-devtool-agent.ts` | React hook managing PageAgent lifecycle |

## Notes

- `next.config.ts` has `typescript: { ignoreBuildErrors: true }` — TypeScript errors won't fail the build, but type correctness still matters for maintainability.
- ESLint is configured very permissively (most rules disabled) — don't rely on lint to catch issues.
- `reactStrictMode: false` — effects run once in dev.
- The `examples/` directory contains development task prompts/worklog artifacts, not source code.
- There is no Prisma, no SQLite, no `db/` directory. All persistence is `localStorage` only.

input.content:
# Implement the Claude Design `Dashboard` and `SQL Editor` screens

## Context

Two screens were designed in the Claude Design project
`b40da1c8-8291-492e-92bc-1ff82119a972` against the Supabase design system
(`supabase-design-system-d9c052fa`) and now need to land in the app:
`Dashboard.dc.html` and `SQL Editor.dc.html`.

Both current panels drifted from that design in the same direction: they are
stacks of full-width shadcn `Card`s with generous padding, where the design is
dense, grid-based, and information-first.

- `src/components/project-dashboard.tsx` is a vertical stack of five collapsible
  cards, each embedding a whole feature component. The design is a 12-column
  grid of five summary cards that answer "is anything wrong" in one screen and
  link out for detail.
- `src/components/sql-panel.tsx` is a single stacked editor card. The design is a
  full-height three-region IDE: schema browser rail, tabbed editor, docked
  results.

The design's colour and type values are already in the codebase — `globals.css`
carries the same Supabase DS HSL tokens (`--background-surface-75`,
`--foreground-lighter`, `--border-default`, `--brand-supabase`, …) mapped onto
Tailwind's `bg-card` / `text-muted-foreground` / `border-border` / `text-primary`.
So this is layout and density work, not a re-theme. One gap: the DS
`--code-block-1..5` syntax colours are **not** in `globals.css` and must be added.

Two scope decisions were confirmed with Jesse:

1. **Dashboard** — build the grid as the top of the page and keep the existing
   deep sections below it, collapsed by default. `LatencyMonitor`,
   `SecurityScore` and `IndexViewer` have no other home in the nav, so removing
   them would delete working features.
2. **SQL Editor** — build everything except the `⌘K` agent prompt bar. `⌘K` is
   already the command palette (`src/components/command-palette.tsx:68`).

---

## Part 1 — Dashboard

### File: `src/components/project-dashboard.tsx` (rewrite of the render body)

**Header row** replaces the `Project Overview` card. One line: project name +
health `Badge` (`healthStatus.status` → Healthy/Degraded/Unhealthy), mono
project ref underneath; right side is Postgres version, created date, the
project URL as a link, and the existing `fetchProjectInfo` Refresh button. All
values already exist as `displayName` / `displayRef` / `displayDbVersion` /
`displayCreatedAt` / `displayUrl`.

**The grid** — `grid grid-cols-12 gap-4`, cards `bg-card border border-border
rounded-lg`:

| Card | Span | Content | Data source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Security | 5 | Big score `/ 100`, "Policy coverage" progress bar, three status rows (fully protected / RLS-but-no-policies / no RLS) with a `Add policies` button on the warning row | `calculateScore(rlsStatuses, tables)` — **reuse the export** from `src/components/security-score.tsx:43` |
| Indexes | 4 | count / total size / total scans triplet, unused-index warning callout, "Most scanned" top-3 bar list | new `/api/database/indexes` fetch (see below) |
| Latency | 3 | sparkline `<svg>` over the history, avg/min/max triplet, `Ping` button | `latencyHistory` from the store |
| Connection health | 7 | 2-column list of the four checks with pass/warn icons | existing `healthStatus.checks` |
| Database | 5 | tables / RLS policies / functions triplet, footer line with the most recent activity | existing `displayStats`, `activityLog[0]` |

**Links out**: `Open RLS →` calls `setActivePanel('rls')` from the store.
`Open viewer →` and `Activity log →` set the matching section open and
`scrollIntoView` its anchor.

**Below the grid**: the same five `Collapsible` sections as today
(LatencyMonitor, SecurityScore, IndexViewer, Connection info, Recent activity),
with their `useState` defaults flipped from `true` to `false`.

**New data**: the Indexes card needs aggregates the dashboard does not fetch.
Add a `fetchIndexes` callback calling `apiFetch('/api/database/indexes', …)` —
the same endpoint `IndexViewer` uses (`src/components/index-viewer.tsx:377`) —
and derive count, summed size, summed scans, `scans === 0` count and the top 3
by scans. `IndexViewer` is left untouched; it fetches the same endpoint
independently. That is one duplicated request on this panel, and far smaller
than lifting index state into the store.

**New local helper**: a `Metric({ value, unit, label })` for the mono
number + small-unit + caption triplets that appear in three cards.
`StatTile` is not a fit (it is an icon card with different proportions).

---

## Part 2 — SQL Editor

### File: `src/components/sql-panel.tsx`

Root becomes a fixed-height IDE frame instead of a content-height stack:
`flex flex-col h-[calc(100vh-150px)] min-h-[560px]`. The page shell
(`src/app/page.tsx:1740`) is `flex-1 overflow-y-auto` with a `py-4` container
and a `h-14` top bar, so the panel sizes itself; no change to `page.tsx`.

**1. Module header** — SQL icon + label, then the Query runner / Migrations /
Analyzer `TabsList` restyled as the design's segmented control (inset
`bg-secondary` track, `rounded-md`, active pill), and the existing
"Management API access — use with caution" warning pushed right. Same `Tabs`
values, same `MigrationRunner` / `QueryAnalyzer` children.

**2. Schema browser rail** — new, `w-[272px] shrink-0 border-r`, inside the
Query runner tab:
- Search input filtering tables and column names.
- Schema row: `public · {tables.length} tables`.
- Table list from the store's `tables` (`TableSchema[]`, already has
  `columns: ColumnInfo[]` and `foreignKeys`). Expanding a table lists its
  columns with `data_type`; a column appearing in `foreignKeys` gets the key
  icon. Collapsed rows show the column count. Long lists cap at ~30 rows with a
  "N more tables…" line, matching the design.
- AI functions section: fetch `/api/database/views-functions` and keep
  `functions` whose `name` starts with `ai_`, rendering `name` and
  `arguments → return_type`. Hidden when none are found. In demo mode use the
  five names the panel already demos (`ai_summary`, `ai_classify`,
  `ai_sentiment`, `ai_extract`, `ai_embed`).
- Insert behaviour: every row is `draggable` with
  `dataTransfer.setData('text/plain', name)` — a textarea accepts a plain-text
  drop natively, so no drop handler is needed — and a click inserts at the
  caret. Footer hint matches: "Drag or click a table, column, or function to
  insert it".

**3. Editor tabs** — a `useState` array of `{ id, name, sql }` buffers plus an
active id, replacing the single `query` string. `+` opens `untitled-N.sql`;
the `×` closes (the last tab cannot close). `sqlEditorContent` from the store
(pushed by the Policy Generator) opens into the active buffer exactly as it
does today. Buffers stay component state, matching today's behaviour — the
panel unmounts on nav change either way.

**4. Syntax highlighting** — a `<pre>` layer behind a transparent `Textarea`,
both sharing font/size/line-height and scroll position. A ~25-line regex
tokenizer covers keywords, strings, numbers, functions and known table names
(from the store's `tables`, which is what makes `person` and `concept` colour
differently in the design).
Add the five DS syntax tokens to `src/app/globals.css`, in the `:root` and
`.dark` blocks alongside the other DS tokens, plus a `.sql-hl .kw/.fn/.str/
.num/.tbl` rule set:
`--code-block-1: 170.8deg 43.1% 61.4%` (identifiers/tables),
`-2: 33.2deg 90.3% 75.7%` (strings/numbers),
`-3: 83.8deg 61.7% 63.1%` (functions),
`-4: 276.1deg 67.7% 74.5%` (keywords),
`-5: 13.8deg 89.7% 69.6%`, with the light-theme values from the DS
`colors.css`. The existing `.code-block .kw/.fn/.str/.num` rules are a
different (EM neon) palette used elsewhere and are left alone.

**5. Editor toolbar** — right-aligned `Format` / `Templates ▾` / `AI demos ▾` /
`Run ⌘⏎`. `Templates` keeps the existing `QUICK_TEMPLATES` `Select`;
`AI demos` moves today's inline button row (and its OpenAI / Supabase AI
provider toggle) into a dropdown, so the toolbar stays one line. `Format` is a
small local normalizer (uppercase keywords, newline before major clauses) —
no new dependency; the repo has no SQL formatter and this does not warrant one.

**6. Results dock** — bottom region, `border-t bg-card`: status row
(check/x icon, "Query executed", `N rows · M ms`, then Visualize / Copy / CSV /
JSON), the result grid restyled as a mono `grid` with column headers rather
than the shadcn `Table`, and a footer line `Query history {n}` +
`Read-only role · Management API`. All existing handlers (`handleExportCSV`,
`handleExportJSON`, `copyToClipboard`, `QueryChart`) are reused unchanged.
Execution timing is new: record `performance.now()` around the fetch in
`executeQuery` to fill the `· M ms`.

---

## Out of scope

- The `⌘K` agent prompt bar (shortcut collision with the command palette).
- Persisting editor tabs across panel switches (today's single buffer is not
  persisted either).
- Refactoring `IndexViewer` / `LatencyMonitor` to share state with the
  dashboard.

## Verification

- `bunx tsc --noEmit` and `bunx biome check` on the touched files (repo has a
  large pre-existing tsc baseline — compare, don't expect zero).
- `bun run build` compiles.
- `PORT=3002 bun dev`, then with `agent-browser`:
  - **Demo mode** (no connection needed): Dashboard grid renders all five cards
    with demo tables/RLS; SQL panel shows the schema rail populated from
    `DEMO_TABLES`, tabs open/close, dragging a table name into the editor
    inserts it, a demo query runs and fills the results dock.
  - **Live** against `jqjaisrrpoemnrnevmvf` via `/api/seed-connection`: the
    Indexes card shows real counts against what the expanded Index viewer
    section lists, Connection health matches `/api/connections/[id]/health`,
    and the AI functions section lists the real `ai_*` functions.
- Check both themes — the light palette must not be forgotten when adding the
  `--code-block-*` tokens.
- Screenshot each panel and compare against `Dashboard.dc.html` /
  `SQL Editor.dc.html` rendered from the design project.

# Observability panels: move to MCP `query_logs` + advisors

## Context

All three observability panels are broken, for three separate reasons — verified live against project
`jqjaisrrpoemnrnevmvf` using `SEED_ACCESS_TOKEN`:

1. **Supabase removed the MCP `get_logs` tool.** The live tool list is now
   `search_docs, list_tables, list_extensions, list_migrations, apply_migration, execute_sql,
   query_logs, get_advisors, get_project_url, get_publishable_keys, generate_typescript_types,
   list_edge_functions, get_edge_function, deploy_edge_function, create_branch, …` — no `get_logs`.
   `src/app/api/logs/route.ts:145` still calls it, so every Logs-panel fetch and every Traces
   "correlated server logs" fetch 502s. The replacement is `query_logs`: read-only **ClickHouse SQL**
   against one unified `logs` table (`id, timestamp, event_message, severity_text, source,
   log_attributes` map), with `iso_timestamp_start` / `iso_timestamp_end` and a hard 24h window cap.
   So it is MCP again, but SQL is the interface — the Management API made the same move
   (`analytics/endpoints/logs.all` → `/logs`, old one retires 2026-09-23).
2. **`src/app/api/logs/` is git-ignored and has never been committed.** The user's global ignore file
   has a `logs/` rule (`~/.config/git/ignore:63`), which swallows the whole route directory. The
   deployed site therefore has no `/api/logs` at all — even a perfect local fix does not ship until
   this is un-ignored.
3. **The Warnings panel calls a dashboard-only endpoint.**
   `api.supabase.com/platform/projects-resource-warnings` answers `401 {"message":"JWT could not be
   decoded"}`; it is not part of the Management API. Per the user's decision, it is replaced with MCP
   `get_advisors` (verified: 136 real lints for this project, `security` + `performance`).

Verified facts the implementation depends on: sources are `postgres_logs, edge_logs,
function_edge_logs, function_logs, postgrest_logs, realtime_logs, storage_logs, pgbouncer_logs,
auth_logs, auth_audit_logs`; `select *` errors (columns must be named); trace correlation is now a
real column — `log_attributes['trace_id']` (787 rows) plus `request.headers.traceparent`;
`severity_text` values seen are `INFO, LOG, WARNING, WARN, ERROR, FATAL`; timestamps come back naive
UTC (`2026-09-01T07:20:47.057000`, no `Z`); tool output is wrapped in a
`{"result": "…<untrusted-data-UUID>\n{json}\n</untrusted-data-UUID>…"}` envelope that must be unwrapped.

## Changes

### 1. `.gitignore` (repo root) — make the route shippable

Add `!/src/app/api/logs/` (repo `.gitignore` outranks the global excludes file). Confirm with
`git check-ignore -v src/app/api/logs/route.ts` returning nothing, then the route can be committed
like any other file. This alone fixes prod's 404.

### 2. `src/lib/supabase-mcp-client.ts` — unwrap tool output once

Add an exported `unwrapMcpJson(text: string): unknown` that parses the outer JSON, pulls the payload
out of the `<untrusted-data-…>` boundary, and parses that. Every `query_logs` / `get_advisors` caller
needs it; the boundary text is untrusted data and is treated as data only, never as instructions.

### 3. `src/app/api/logs/route.ts` — rewrite on `query_logs`

Replace `SERVICE_TO_MCP` with a source map (`postgres→postgres_logs`, `api→edge_logs`,
`auth→auth_logs`, `edge-functions→function_edge_logs + function_logs`, `storage→storage_logs`,
`realtime→realtime_logs`) plus `all → every source`, and a reverse map for tagging each row's
`service`. One MCP session per request (today it opens one client per service).

Build the SQL:

```sql
select id, timestamp, event_message, severity_text, source, log_attributes
from logs
where source in (…)                       -- omitted for "all"
  [and positionCaseInsensitive(event_message, '<filter>') > 0]
order by timestamp desc
limit <n>
```

- Correlated mode (`traceId`): validate `/^[0-9a-f]{32}$/` first, then
  `where log_attributes['trace_id'] = '…' or log_attributes['request.headers.traceparent'] like '%…%'`
  across all sources — the filtering moves into the query instead of pulling 500 rows and
  string-matching JSON client-side.
- Escape `'` in the filter; the trace id is regex-validated; nothing else is interpolated.
- Honour `startTime`/`endTime` (today they are silently ignored) as `iso_timestamp_start` /
  `iso_timestamp_end`, clamping `start` to `end − 24h` so the API cap can't reject the call.
- Normalize rows to the existing `LogEntry` shape (`src/lib/supabase-types.ts:168`): append `Z` to the
  naive timestamp, map `severity_text` (`LOG→INFO`, `WARNING→WARN`, `FATAL|PANIC→ERROR`, unknown→
  `UNKNOWN`) — replacing the current `detectSeverity` JSON-substring guesswork — `metadata` =
  `log_attributes`, `service` = reverse-mapped source.
- Keep the existing demo-mode short-circuit, auth/403 messages, and token sanitising.

### 4. Logs panel — "All services" default

`src/components/logs-panel.tsx`: add `all` to the service selector and make it the default;
`LogService` in `src/lib/supabase-types.ts` gains `'all'`. Show the per-row source when the view spans
services (each `LogEntry` already carries `service`).

### 5. Warnings panel → advisors

- New `src/app/api/advisors/route.ts`: MCP `get_advisors` for both `security` and `performance`,
  returning the lint list (`name, title, level, categories, description, detail, remediation,
  metadata`). Same `getConnectionFromHeaders` + demo short-circuit shape as the other routes.
- Rewrite `src/components/resource-warnings-panel.tsx` around lints: counts by level (ERROR/WARN/INFO)
  as `StatTile`s (`src/components/ui/stat-tile.tsx`), grouped by lint name, each row showing `detail`
  and a remediation link; a security/performance toggle.
- `src/lib/demo-data.ts`: replace `DEMO_RESOURCE_WARNINGS` with a handful of demo lints; drop
  `ResourceWarning` / `ResourceSeverity` from `src/lib/supabase-types.ts` and delete
  `src/app/api/resource-warnings/route.ts` (nothing else references them).
- Keep the panel's nav label "Warnings".

### 6. Traces panel

No API change needed beyond §3 — it calls `/api/logs` with `traceId`. Verify the correlated-logs
section now returns rows for a live propagated trace.

## Verification

- `bun test`, `bunx tsc --noEmit` (touched files only — the repo has a large pre-existing baseline),
  `bunx biome check` on touched files, `bun run build`.
- Unit check for the pure parts, in the style of the existing
  `src/app/api/iceberg/tables/extract-stats.test.ts`: SQL builder (source mapping, filter escaping,
  trace-id rejection of non-hex input, 24h clamp) and the row → `LogEntry` normalizer.
- Live end-to-end against Prom Labs with the seed connection (`/api/seed-connection` prefills from
  `.env`): Logs panel returns rows for "All services" and each individual service, the time-range
  selector changes the result set, and search filters server-side; Warnings panel lists real advisors;
  Traces panel shows correlated logs for a fresh propagated trace id.
- `git check-ignore -v src/app/api/logs/route.ts` prints nothing, and `git status` shows the route as
  a new untracked file ready to commit.

32	export interface ScoreBreakdown {
33	  score: number
34	  tablesWithoutRLS: TableRLSInfo[]
35	  tablesWithRLSNoPolicies: TableRLSInfo[]
36	  tablesFullyProtected: TableRLSInfo[]
37	  restrictivePolicies: number
38	  tablesOnlySelect: TableRLSInfo[]
39	  policyCoverage: number
40	  criticalTables: TableRLSInfo[]
41	}
42	
43	export function calculateScore(rlsStatuses: TableRLSInfo[], tables: TableSchema[]): ScoreBreakdown {
44	  let score = 100
45	  let restrictivePolicies = 0
46	
47	  const tablesWithoutRLS = rlsStatuses.filter((t) => !t.rlsEnabled)
48	  const tablesWithRLSNoPolicies = rlsStatuses.filter((t) => t.rlsEnabled && t.policies.length === 0)
49	  const tablesFullyProtected = rlsStatuses.filter((t) => t.rlsEnabled && t.policies.length > 0)
50	
51	  // -20 for each table without RLS enabled
52	  score -= tablesWithoutRLS.length * 20
53	
54	  // -5 for each table with RLS enabled but no policies
55	  score -= tablesWithRLSNoPolicies.length * 5
56	
57	  // -3 for each RESTRICTIVE policy
58	  rlsStatuses.forEach((t) => {
59	    t.policies.forEach((p) => {
60	      if (p.permissive === 'RESTRICTIVE') {
61	        restrictivePolicies++
62	        score -= 3
63	      }
64	    })
65	  })
66	
67	  // -2 for each table with only SELECT policies (missing INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE protection)
68	  const tablesOnlySelect = rlsStatuses.filter((t) => {
69	    if (!t.rlsEnabled || t.policies.length === 0) return false
70	    const commands = new Set(t.policies.map((p) => p.cmd))
71	    return (
72	      commands.has('SELECT') &&
73	      !commands.has('INSERT') &&
74	      !commands.has('UPDATE') &&
75	      !commands.has('DELETE') &&
76	      !commands.has('ALL')
77	    )
78	  })
79	  score -= tablesOnlySelect.length * 2
80	
81	  // Cap at 0
82	  score = Math.max(0, score)
83	
84	  // Policy coverage: percentage of operations covered by at least one policy
85	  const totalOperations = rlsStatuses.length * 4 // SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE per table
86	  let coveredOperations = 0
87	  rlsStatuses.forEach((t) => {
88	    if (!t.rlsEnabled) return // Tables without RLS don't count towards "covered"
89	    const commands = new Set(t.policies.map((p) => p.cmd))
90	    if (commands.has('SELECT') || commands.has('ALL')) coveredOperations++
91	    if (commands.has('INSERT') || commands.has('ALL')) coveredOperations++
92	    if (commands.has('UPDATE') || commands.has('ALL')) coveredOperations++
93	    if (commands.has('DELETE') || commands.has('ALL')) coveredOperations++
94	  })
95	  const policyCoverage =
96	    totalOperations > 0 ? Math.round((coveredOperations / totalOperations) * 100) : 0
97	
98	  // Critical: Tables without RLS that have foreign keys to protected tables
99	  const protectedTableNames = new Set(tablesFullyProtected.map((t) => t.tableName))
100	  const criticalTables = tablesWithoutRLS.filter((t) => {
101	    const tableSchema = tables.find((ts) => ts.tableName === t.tableName)
102	    if (!tableSchema) return false
103	    return tableSchema.foreignKeys.some((fk) => protectedTableNames.has(fk.foreign_table_name))
104	  })
105	
106	  return {
107	    score,
108	    tablesWithoutRLS,
109	    tablesWithRLSNoPolicies,
110	    tablesFullyProtected,
111	    restrictivePolicies,
112	    tablesOnlySelect,
113	    policyCoverage,
114	    criticalTables,
115	  }
116	}
117	
118	function getScoreColor(score: number): string {
119	  if (score >= 80) return 'text-primary'
120	  if (score >= 60) return 'text-amber-500'
121	  if (score >= 40) return 'text-orange-500'
122	  return 'text-red-500'
123	}
124	
125	function getScoreStroke(score: number): string {
126	  if (score >= 80) return '#10b981'
127	  if (score >= 60) return '#f59e0b'
128	  if (score >= 40) return '#f97316'
129	  return '#ef4444'
130	}

## Dashboard

The stack of full-width collapsibles becomes the design's 12-column at-a-glance grid: **Security** (score, policy coverage, RLS breakdown with an Add-policies action), **Indexes** (counts, unused-index callout, most-scanned bars), **Latency** (sparkline, avg/min/max, Ping), **Connection health** and **Database**.

A full-height three-region IDE: schema browser rail, tabbed editor, docked results.

content.text:
Both designs are implemented, verified live, and up as **[PR #14](https://github.com/JesseVent/supabasehire.me/pull/14)** on `feat/design-dashboard-sql`.

**Dashboard** — the 12-column grid replaces the collapsible stack. Security card reuses the exported `calculateScore()` so it can't drift from the detail panel below it; Indexes pulls `/api/database/indexes` for its aggregates; Latency shares a new `useLatencyPing()` hook with the monitor rather than duplicating the fetch. The three deep components sit below, collapsed, because the grid's links are their only route in.

**SQL Editor** — full-height IDE. Schema rail (search, expandable columns with short types, FK markers, real `ai_*` functions, drag-or-click to insert), multiple `.sql` buffers, syntax highlighting off the DS `--code-block-*` tokens, and the docked results grid with rows + elapsed ms.

Live against `jqjaisrrpoemnrnevmvf`: 88 indexes / 7.7 GB / 14.4M scans, 64 unused reclaiming ~4.6 GB, four health checks, nine `ai_*` functions, real query returning rows. Both themes checked. 15 tests pass, tsc at the 94-error baseline, build compiles.

- **`⌘K` agent bar skipped** — `⌘K` is already the command palette (`command-palette.tsx:68`). Everything else in the design shipped.
- **Also fixed:** the dashboard header was printing `Postgres —` and a literal `unknown` region; it now drops facts the project API doesn't know. And `applyTemplate`/`runAiDemo` would have written to the wrong buffer after a tab switch — caught by the dep-array lint, fixed before it shipped.
- **Your dev server was serving a stale Turbopack build** — `.next/cache` wasn't enough, the CSS changes only appeared after wiping `.next` entirely. Worth remembering when a globals.css edit seems to do nothing.

content.text:
Now it's actually verified. This round found and fixed one real bug.

**Newly tested:**
- **AI demos dropdown** — provider toggle flips state and keeps the menu open; selecting a demo set the SQL, executed it, and rendered the error path in the dock. **Found a bug**: 12 entries overflowed a short viewport. Fixed by clamping to `--radix-dropdown-menu-content-available-height`; confirmed at 620px it now clamps and scrolls. Pushed as `704d490`.
- **Migrations tab** — templates and editor render and scroll in the new container.
- **Analyzer tab** — renders, and correctly received the active buffer's SQL, so `query` still flows out of the tabbed state.
- **Templates dropdown** — writes into the active buffer.
- **`/` shortcut** — focuses the schema search. It failed on my first attempt, but that was a leftover Radix Select focus scope from the Templates dropdown I'd opened a moment earlier; on clean state it works.
- **Drag** — 39 draggable rows, and `dragstart` sets `text/plain` to the right identifier.

**Still not directly observed:**
- **The drop itself.** I verified the payload my code sets; the insertion into the textarea is native browser behaviour I asserted rather than watched. If you want that guaranteed rather than relied upon, an explicit `onDrop` handler would make it deterministic — say the word.
- **CSV / JSON / Copy / Visualize** — those handlers are unchanged from before, only restyled, so I treated them as existing behaviour rather than new risk. That's a judgement call, not a test.

One thing worth flagging from the demo run: it failed with `provider=supabase is local-only`. That's the app behaving correctly on hosted Supabase, not a regression — I'd toggled to Supabase AI. I didn't re-run on OpenAI because that spends an API call.
